req.title: Reuse db connection per request
req.statement: The system shall reuse a single sqlite3 connection per Flask request via flask.g.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-025 requires that a single sqlite3 connection is reused per Flask request via flask.g. The key invariant is: within one request context, get_db() called multiple times returns the SAME connection object (identity check). Across separate requests, connections may differ. We test: (1) positive — two get_db() calls in one request context return identical objects; (2) negative — connections from two separate request contexts are distinct objects; (3) boundary — the 'db' key is absent from g before first call and present after, and close_db() removes it (state transition at the boundary of request lifecycle). Additional tests cover the teardown path and the exact sqlite3.Row row_factory assignment.

tests.name: test_get_db_returns_same_connection_within_single_request
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
A single request context is active
actions: Push an application context
Call get_db() twice within the same context
Compare the two returned connection objects with 'is'
expected: Both calls return the exact same sqlite3.Connection object (identity)
g.db is set after the first call
trace: R-FLASKR-025: single connection per request reused via flask.g
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_get_db_same_connection_within_request():
    with app.app_context():
        conn1 = get_db()
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert conn1 is conn2, 'get_db() must return the same object on repeated calls'
        from flask import g
        assert 'db' in g, 'g must contain db key after get_db() call'

test_get_db_same_connection_within_request()

tests.name: test_get_db_returns_different_connections_across_requests
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
Two separate request contexts are used
actions: Push first application context, call get_db(), record id, pop context
Push second application context, call get_db(), record id, pop context
Compare the two connection ids
expected: The two connection objects are NOT the same instance (different ids)
Each context has its own independent g.db
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection is per-request, not shared across requests
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_get_db_different_connections_across_requests():
    with app.app_context():
        conn1_id = id(get_db())
    with app.app_context():
        conn2_id = id(get_db())
    assert conn1_id != conn2_id, 'Separate request contexts must not share a connection'

test_get_db_different_connections_across_requests()

tests.name: test_close_db_removes_db_from_g_boundary
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
A single application context is active
actions: Verify 'db' not in g before any get_db() call
Call get_db() — 'db' must now be in g
Call close_db() — 'db' must be removed from g
Call close_db() again with no db in g — must not raise
expected: 'db' absent from g before first get_db()
Second close_db() call is idempotent (no exception)
trace: R-FLASKR-025: boundary of request lifecycle — g.db created on first access, removed on teardown
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, close_db, init_db
from flask import g

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_close_db_boundary():
    with app.app_context():
        assert 'db' not in g, 'db must not be in g before get_db()'
        get_db()
        assert 'db' in g, 'db must be in g after get_db()'
        close_db()
        assert 'db' not in g, 'db must be removed from g after close_db()'
        try:
            close_db()
        except Exception as exc:
            raise AssertionError(f'close_db() must be idempotent, raised: {exc}')

test_close_db_boundary()

actions: Push an application context

import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_get_db_row_factory():
    with app.app_context():
        conn = get_db()
        assert conn.row_factory is sqlite3.Row, (
            f'row_factory must be sqlite3.Row, got {conn.row_factory}'
        )

tests.name: test_teardown_closes_connection_after_request
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Make a GET request to /hello via test client
Verify 200 response
Confirm teardown ran by checking that a second request also succeeds (connection was properly closed and not leaked)
expected: First GET /hello returns 200 with body 'Hello, World!'
Second GET /hello also returns 200 (teardown did not corrupt state)
trace: R-FLASKR-025: close_db registered via teardown_appcontext; each request gets fresh connection
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_teardown_closes_connection():
    r1 = client.get('/hello')
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert r1.data == b'Hello, World!'
    r2 = client.get('/hello')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r2.data == b'Hello, World!'

test_teardown_closes_connection()

tests.name: test_get_db_connection_is_open_and_usable
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
Database initialised with init_db() so user table exists
actions: Push an application context
Call get_db()
Execute a simple SELECT against the user table
Fetch results and verify known fixture data
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection returned by get_db() must be live and functional
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_get_db_connection_usable():
    with app.app_context():
        conn = get_db()
        rows = conn.execute('SELECT id, username FROM user ORDER BY id').fetchall()
        assert len(rows) == 2, f'Expected 2 users, got {len(rows)}'
        assert rows[0]['id'] == 1
        assert rows[0]['username'] == 'test'
        assert rows[1]['id'] == 2
        assert rows[1]['username'] == 'other'

test_get_db_connection_usable()

tests.name: test_get_db_not_called_before_request_g_has_no_db
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
A fresh application context just pushed (get_db never called)
actions: Push a fresh application context without calling get_db()
Check that 'db' is NOT in flask.g
expected: 'db' key is absent from g at the start of a context (before any get_db call)
g.pop('db', None) returns None — same as close_db sentinel
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection only created on first get_db() call, not eagerly
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flask import g

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

def test_g_has_no_db_before_get_db():
    with app.app_context():
        assert 'db' not in g, 'g.db must not exist before get_db() is called'
        sentinel = g.pop('db', None)
        assert sentinel is None, (
            f'g.pop("db", None) must return None before get_db(), got {sentinel}'
        )

test_g_has_no_db_before_get_db()
